review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

14:1.sourceText: Μὴ ταρασσέσθω ὑμῶν ἡ καρδία· πιστεύετε εἰς τὸν Θεόν, καὶ εἰς ἐμὲ πιστεύετε.
14:1.targetText: “Do not let your hearts be troubled. You believe in God; believe in Me as well.

groups.note: The third-person imperative supplies Do … let and be troubled.
The same form πιστεύετε is read here as a statement and later in the verse as a command.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

14:2.sourceText: ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ τοῦ Πατρός μου μοναὶ πολλαί εἰσιν· εἰ δὲ μή, εἶπον ἂν ὑμῖν· ὅτι πορεύομαι ἑτοιμάσαι τόπον ὑμῖν·
14:2.targetText: In My Father’s house are many rooms. If it were not so, would I have told you that I am going there to prepare a place for you?

groups.note: εἰ δὲ μή ("but if not", otherwise) is rendered If it were not so.
ἄν with the aorist marks the unreal result, would have.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds there to point back to the Father’s house.

14:3.sourceText: καὶ ἐὰν πορευθῶ καὶ ἑτοιμάσω τόπον ὑμῖν, πάλιν ἔρχομαι καὶ παραλήμψομαι ὑμᾶς πρὸς ἐμαυτόν, ἵνα ὅπου εἰμὶ ἐγὼ καὶ ὑμεῖς ἦτε.
14:3.targetText: And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come back and welcome you into My presence, so that you also may be where I am.

groups.note: πάλιν ("again") is rendered back.
ἐμαυτόν ("Myself") is rendered My presence.

14:4.sourceText: καὶ ὅπου ἐγὼ ὑπάγω οἴδατε τὴν ὁδόν.
14:4.targetText: You know the way to the place where I am going.”

groups.note: The relative ὅπου ("where") includes its implied antecedent, rendered to the place where.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening connective καί untranslated.

14:5.sourceText: Λέγει αὐτῷ Θωμᾶς Κύριε, οὐκ οἴδαμεν ποῦ ὑπάγεις· πῶς οἴδαμεν τὴν ὁδὸν;
14:5.targetText: “Lord,” said Thomas, “we do not know where You are going, so how can we know the way?”

groups.note: BSB's Greek differs slightly here, but know still renders this verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The indirect object αὐτῷ ("to Him") is not rendered.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds so; the Greek has no connective here.
BSB follows a reading with an extra word here, rendered can.

14:6.sourceText: λέγει αὐτῷ Ἰησοῦς Ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ὁδὸς καὶ ἡ ἀλήθεια καὶ ἡ ζωή· οὐδεὶς ἔρχεται πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα εἰ μὴ δι’ ἐμοῦ.
14:6.targetText: Jesus answered, “I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me.

groups.note: εἰ μή ("if not") together supply except.

unmappedSource.reason: The indirect object αὐτῷ ("to him") is not rendered.

14:7.sourceText: εἰ ἐγνώκειτέ με, καὶ τὸν Πατέρα μου ἂν ᾔδειτε· ἀπ’ ἄρτι γινώσκετε αὐτὸν καὶ ἑωράκατε.
14:7.targetText: If you had known Me, you would know My Father as well. From now on you do know Him and have seen Him.”

groups.note: ἄν with ᾔδειτε marks the unreal result, would know.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows a reading with an extra word here, rendered Him.

14:8.sourceText: Λέγει αὐτῷ Φίλιππος Κύριε, δεῖξον ἡμῖν τὸν Πατέρα, καὶ ἀρκεῖ ἡμῖν.
14:8.targetText: Philip said to Him, “Lord, show us the Father, and that will be enough for us.”

14:9.sourceText: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Τοσοῦτον χρόνον μεθ’ ὑμῶν εἰμι καὶ οὐκ ἔγνωκάς με, Φίλιππε; ὁ ἑωρακὼς ἐμὲ ἑώρακεν τὸν Πατέρα· πῶς σὺ λέγεις Δεῖξον ἡμῖν τὸν Πατέρα;
14:9.targetText: Jesus replied, “Philip, I have been with you all this time, and still you do not know Me? Anyone who has seen Me has seen the Father. How can you say, ‘Show us the Father’?

groups.note: Τοσοῦτον χρόνον ("so long a time") is rendered all this time; BSB's Greek differs slightly here, with the same sense.
The present εἰμι ("I am") is rendered I have been.
Article and participle ὁ ἑωρακώς form one unit.

unmappedSource.reason: The indirect object αὐτῷ ("to him") is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds still; the Greek has only καί ("and").
English adds can; the Greek has only λέγεις ("you say").

14:10.sourceText: οὐ πιστεύεις ὅτι ἐγὼ ἐν τῷ Πατρὶ καὶ ὁ Πατὴρ ἐν ἐμοί ἐστιν; τὰ ῥήματα ἃ ἐγὼ λέγω ὑμῖν ἀπ’ ἐμαυτοῦ οὐ λαλῶ· ὁ δὲ Πατὴρ ἐν ἐμοὶ μένων ποιεῖ τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ.
14:10.targetText: Do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in Me? The words I say to you, I do not speak on My own. Instead, it is the Father dwelling in Me, performing His works.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the relative pronoun ἅ ("which") unexpressed.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula for the first clause; ἐστιν stands with the second (the Father is in Me).
English recasts the sentence with it is; the Greek has none here.

14:11.sourceText: πιστεύετέ μοι ὅτι ἐγὼ ἐν τῷ Πατρὶ καὶ ὁ Πατὴρ ἐν ἐμοί· εἰ δὲ μή, διὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτὰ πιστεύετε.
14:11.targetText: Believe Me that I am in the Father and the Father is in Me—or at least believe on account of the works themselves.

groups.note: εἰ δὲ μή ("but if not", otherwise) is rendered or at least.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula; the Greek clause has no verb.
English supplies the copula; the Greek clause has no verb.

14:12.sourceText: ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ὁ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμὲ τὰ ἔργα ἃ ἐγὼ ποιῶ κἀκεῖνος ποιήσει, καὶ μείζονα τούτων ποιήσει, ὅτι ἐγὼ πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα πορεύομαι·
14:12.targetText: Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever believes in Me will also do the works that I am doing. He will do even greater things than these, because I am going to the Father.

groups.note: Article and participle ὁ πιστεύων form one unit.
κἀκεῖνος ("that one also") is rendered also.

14:13.sourceText: καὶ ὅ τι ἂν αἰτήσητε ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μου, τοῦτο ποιήσω, ἵνα δοξασθῇ ὁ Πατὴρ ἐν τῷ Υἱῷ.
14:13.targetText: And I will do whatever you ask in My name, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son.

groups.note: ὅ τι ἄν ("whatever") works as one unit; BSB's Greek differs slightly here, with the same sense.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the resumptive τοῦτο ("this") unexpressed.

14:14.sourceText: ἐάν τι αἰτήσητέ με ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μου, ἐγὼ ποιήσω.
14:14.targetText: If you ask Me for anything in My name, I will do it.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object; ποιήσω has none.

14:15.sourceText: Ἐὰν ἀγαπᾶτέ με, τὰς ἐντολὰς τὰς ἐμὰς τηρήσετε.
14:15.targetText: If you love Me, you will keep My commandments.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

14:16.sourceText: κἀγὼ ἐρωτήσω τὸν Πατέρα καὶ ἄλλον Παράκλητον δώσει ὑμῖν ἵνα ᾖ μεθ’ ὑμῶν εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα,
14:16.targetText: And I will ask the Father, and He will give you another Advocate to be with you forever—

groups.note: κἀγώ (καί + ἐγώ) is rendered And I.
εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ("into the age") is rendered forever.

14:17.sourceText: τὸ Πνεῦμα τῆς ἀληθείας, ὃ ὁ κόσμος οὐ δύναται λαβεῖν, ὅτι οὐ θεωρεῖ αὐτὸ οὐδὲ γινώσκει· ὑμεῖς γινώσκετε αὐτό, ὅτι παρ’ ὑμῖν μένει καὶ ἐν ὑμῖν ἔσται.
14:17.targetText: the Spirit of truth. The world cannot receive Him, because it neither sees Him nor knows Him. But you do know Him, for He abides with you and will be in you.

groups.note: The relative ὅ ("which") is rendered Him in a new sentence.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object; γινώσκει has none.
English adds a contrast; the Greek has no connective here.

14:18.sourceText: οὐκ ἀφήσω ὑμᾶς ὀρφανούς, ἔρχομαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς.
14:18.targetText: I will not leave you as orphans; I will come to you.

14:19.sourceText: ἔτι μικρὸν καὶ ὁ κόσμος με οὐκέτι θεωρεῖ, ὑμεῖς δὲ θεωρεῖτέ με, ὅτι ἐγὼ ζῶ καὶ ὑμεῖς ζήσετε.
14:19.targetText: In a little while the world will see Me no more, but you will see Me. Because I live, you also will live.

groups.note: ἔτι μικρόν ("yet a little") is rendered In a little while.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves καί untranslated; the time phrase leads straight into the clause.

14:20.sourceText: ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ γνώσεσθε ὑμεῖς ὅτι ἐγὼ ἐν τῷ Πατρί μου καὶ ὑμεῖς ἐν ἐμοὶ κἀγὼ ἐν ὑμῖν.
14:20.targetText: On that day you will know that I am in My Father, and you are in Me, and I am in you.

groups.note: κἀγώ (καί + ἐγώ) is rendered and I.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula; the Greek clause has no verb.
English supplies the copula; the Greek clause has no verb.
English supplies the copula; the Greek clause has no verb.

14:21.sourceText: ὁ ἔχων τὰς ἐντολάς μου καὶ τηρῶν αὐτὰς, ἐκεῖνός ἐστιν ὁ ἀγαπῶν με· ὁ δὲ ἀγαπῶν με ἀγαπηθήσεται ὑπὸ τοῦ Πατρός μου, κἀγὼ ἀγαπήσω αὐτὸν καὶ ἐμφανίσω αὐτῷ ἐμαυτόν.
14:21.targetText: Whoever has My commandments and keeps them is the one who loves Me. The one who loves Me will be loved by My Father, and I will love him and reveal Myself to him.”

groups.note: Article and participle ὁ ἔχων form one unit.
Article and participle ὁ ἀγαπῶν form one unit.
Article and participle ὁ … ἀγαπῶν form one unit.
κἀγώ (καί + ἐγώ) is rendered and I.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The resumptive ἐκεῖνος ("that one") repeats the subject, which English states once.
BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.

14:22.sourceText: Λέγει αὐτῷ Ἰούδας, οὐχ ὁ Ἰσκαριώτης Κύριε, καὶ τί γέγονεν ὅτι ἡμῖν μέλλεις ἐμφανίζειν σεαυτὸν καὶ οὐχὶ τῷ κόσμῳ;
14:22.targetText: Judas (not Iscariot) asked Him, “Lord, why are You going to reveal Yourself to us and not to the world?”

groups.note: τί γέγονεν ὅτι ("what has happened that") is rendered why.
The dative τῷ κόσμῳ supplies to.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves καί untranslated at the start of the question.

14:23.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἐάν τις ἀγαπᾷ, με τὸν λόγον μου τηρήσει, καὶ ὁ Πατήρ μου ἀγαπήσει αὐτόν, καὶ πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐλευσόμεθα καὶ μονὴν παρ’ αὐτῷ ποιησόμεθα.
14:23.targetText: Jesus replied, “If anyone loves Me, he will keep My word. My Father will love him, and We will come to him and make Our home with him.

groups.note: ἀπεκρίθη … καὶ εἶπεν ("answered and said") is rendered by the one verb replied.

unmappedSource.reason: The indirect object αὐτῷ ("to him") is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence here instead of rendering καί.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the possessive; μονήν ("dwelling") has none.

14:24.sourceText: ὁ μὴ ἀγαπῶν με τοὺς λόγους μου οὐ τηρεῖ· καὶ ὁ λόγος ὃν ἀκούετε οὐκ ἔστιν ἐμὸς ἀλλὰ τοῦ πέμψαντός με Πατρός.
14:24.targetText: Whoever does not love Me does not keep My words. The word that you hear is not My own, but it is from the Father who sent Me.

groups.note: Article and participle ὁ … ἀγαπῶν form one unit.
The genitive Πατρός ("of the Father") is rendered from the Father.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence here instead of rendering καί.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject and verb; the Greek has only the genitive phrase.

14:25.sourceText: Ταῦτα λελάληκα ὑμῖν παρ’ ὑμῖν μένων·
14:25.targetText: All this I have spoken to you while I am still with you.

groups.note: The participle μένων ("remaining") is rendered while I am still.

14:26.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Παράκλητος, τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον ὃ πέμψει ὁ Πατὴρ ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μου, ἐκεῖνος ὑμᾶς διδάξει πάντα καὶ ὑπομνήσει ὑμᾶς πάντα ἃ εἶπον ὑμῖν ἐγώ.
14:26.targetText: But the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in My name, will teach you all things and will remind you of everything I have told you.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The resumptive ἐκεῖνος ("that one") repeats the subject, which English states once.
BSB leaves the relative pronoun ἅ ("which") unexpressed.

14:27.sourceText: Εἰρήνην ἀφίημι ὑμῖν, εἰρήνην τὴν ἐμὴν δίδωμι ὑμῖν· οὐ καθὼς ὁ κόσμος δίδωσιν ἐγὼ δίδωμι ὑμῖν. μὴ ταρασσέσθω ὑμῶν ἡ καρδία μηδὲ δειλιάτω.
14:27.targetText: Peace I leave with you; My peace I give to you. I do not give to you as the world gives. Do not let your hearts be troubled; do not be afraid.

groups.note: The third-person imperative supplies Do … let and be troubled.
μηδέ ("nor") is rendered not after the semicolon.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

14:28.sourceText: ἠκούσατε ὅτι ἐγὼ εἶπον ὑμῖν Ὑπάγω καὶ ἔρχομαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς. εἰ ἠγαπᾶτέ με, ἐχάρητε ἄν ὅτι πορεύομαι πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα, ὅτι ὁ Πατὴρ μείζων μού ἐστιν.
14:28.targetText: You heard Me say, ‘I am going away, and I am coming back to you.’ If you loved Me, you would rejoice that I am going to the Father, because the Father is greater than I.

groups.note: The subject ἐγώ of εἶπον ("I said") becomes the object Me in BSB's wording.
ἄν with the aorist marks the unreal result, would.
The genitive μου ("than me") supplies than.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves ὅτι ("that") unexpressed after heard.
BSB leaves ὑμῖν ("to you") unexpressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds back; ἔρχομαι means "I come".

14:29.sourceText: καὶ νῦν εἴρηκα ὑμῖν πρὶν γενέσθαι, ἵνα ὅταν γένηται πιστεύσητε.
14:29.targetText: And now I have told you before it happens, so that when it does happen, you will believe.

14:30.sourceText: οὐκέτι πολλὰ λαλήσω μεθ’ ὑμῶν, ἔρχεται γὰρ ὁ τοῦ κόσμου ἄρχων· καὶ ἐν ἐμοὶ οὐκ ἔχει οὐδέν,
14:30.targetText: I will not speak with you much longer, for the prince of this world is coming, and he has no claim on Me.

groups.note: οὐκέτι ("no longer") is rendered not … longer.
οὐκ … οὐδέν ("not … anything") is rendered no claim.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies this, matching the prince of this world in 12:31 and 16:11; here the Greek has only the article.

14:31.sourceText: ἀλλ’ ἵνα γνῷ ὁ κόσμος ὅτι ἀγαπῶ τὸν Πατέρα, καὶ καθὼς ἐνετείλατο μοι ὁ Πατὴρ, οὕτως ποιῶ. Ἐγείρεσθε, ἄγωμεν ἐντεῦθεν.
14:31.targetText: But I do exactly what the Father has commanded Me, so that the world may know that I love the Father.  Get up! Let us go on from here.

groups.note: καθὼς … οὕτως ("just as … so") is rendered exactly what.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves καί untranslated as it reorders the sentence.
